newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa eases limits on banks' fx holdings - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa eases limits on banks' fx holdings - paper.

text.p: The South African Reserve Bank has in recent months relaxed restrictions on the amount of foreign exchange which may be held by commercial banks, the Financial Mail reported on Thursday.
The paper quoted the central bank's head of international banking, Bertus van Zyl, saying the limit was increased to around $1.4 billion in the latter half of last year.
"We allowed the banks to exceed their limit for some months, then officially increased it in the second half of 1996," van Zyl said.
The limit is not usually made public, but van Zyl said it had stood at around $700 million. "This limit was more or less doubled. But that doesn't mean the banks are utilising all of it."
The banks held an average of around $800 million to April last year and $1.2 billion between April and November, the paper said.
Van Zyl said the primary reason for allowing banks to hold more foreign exchange offshore was because this was necessary to help develop the forward market.
"Obviously, as the (Reserve) Bank is trying to pull out of the forward markets, the banks are being given more leeway to hold foreign currency against forward commitments," he said.
